item.title: 19-year-old wanted after two men found shot to death in Tunica County neighborhood - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUNICA COUNTY – A 19-year-old Tunica man is wanted for questioning after two men were found shot to death in a Tunica County subdivision.

According to the Tunica County Sheriff’s Office, deputies received a 911 call around 7:37 p.m. Sunday, May 24, reporting that someone had hit a tree and appeared to be unresponsive in the White Oak subdivision.

When deputies arrived, they found that both people had been shot.

The victims were identified as 42-year-old Taurean Martez Thomas and 33-year-old David Brown III, both of Tunica. Both men were pronounced dead at the scene by the Tunica County coroner.

The sheriff’s office said 19-year-old Jadarius Antwan Douglas, of Tunica, is wanted for questioning in the double homicide.

The Tunica County Sheriff’s Office Criminal Investigation Division has also obtained warrants for Douglas in connection with additional crimes. Authorities said the warrants include two counts of kidnapping, armed robbery, simple assault and shooting into a motor vehicle.

Officials said it has not been confirmed whether those crimes are related to the double homicide investigation. The investigations remain active and ongoing.

Anyone with information about the homicides is asked to contact Crime Stoppers at 662-910-0400. Information may qualify for a cash reward of up to $2,000.

Information leading to Douglas’ arrest may qualify for a reward of up to $1,000. Tips may also be reported to the Tunica County Sheriff’s Office at 662-363-1411.

item.title: Two injured in Memorial Day shooting in Pearl River County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
PEARL RIVER COUNTY – Two people were injured in a Memorial Day shooting in Pearl River County.

According to the Pearl River County Sheriff’s Department, deputies and investigators responded around 6:30 p.m. Monday, May 25, to a shooting near Lilac Drive and Clover Drive in Picayune.

Investigators said two victims suffered non-life-threatening gunshot wounds.

Witnesses and complainants told authorities that multiple people were at the scene when a physical altercation occurred. During the altercation, numerous shots were fired by more than one gunman, according to the sheriff’s department.

No arrests have been made, and the investigation remains active.

Anyone with information about the shooting is asked to contact the Pearl River County Sheriff’s Department Investigations Division at 601-403-2530. Anonymous tips may also be submitted through Mississippi Coast Crime Stoppers at 1-877-787-5898 or MSCoastCrimeStoppers.com.

item.title: Two injured after shots fired in Columbus - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
COLUMBUS – Two people were injured in a shooting Monday in Columbus, police said.

According to the Columbus Police Department, officers responded May 25 to the 1500 block of 24th Street North in reference to shots fired.

Police said the victims had already been taken by private vehicle to Baptist Memorial Hospital-Golden Triangle before officers arrived.

One victim is listed in stable condition, while the other remains in critical condition, according to police.

The incident remains under active investigation by the Columbus Police Department.

Anyone with information is asked to contact the Columbus Police Department or Golden Triangle Crime Stoppers.

item.title: Tupelo police looking for burglary suspect after $4,000 in items stolen from business - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUPELO – Crime Stoppers of Northeast Mississippi and the Tupelo Police Department are asking for the public’s help identifying a person wanted in connection with a commercial burglary.

According to Crime Stoppers, Tupelo officers responded around 3 a.m. March 22 to an alarm call at The Fox’s Den, located at 1210 S. Gloster St.

When officers arrived, they found broken glass at the front entrance of the business. The owner later arrived and told police that about $4,000 worth of items had been stolen.

The business owner also provided officers with video footage of the incident.

Anyone with information is asked to contact Crime Stoppers of Northeast Mississippi through the P3 Tips app. Crime Stoppers said it may pay up to $2,000 for a tip that leads to an arrest.

The 800 number is temporarily out of service, according to Crime Stoppers.

item.title: Pilots eject safely after Navy plane crash near Kemper, Noxubee county line - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Cash Matlock
item.description:
NOXUBEE COUNTY – Two pilots safely ejected after a Navy plane crashed Tuesday near the Kemper and Noxubee county line, authorities said.

Kemper County Sheriff James Moore confirmed the crash happened near the Tanner Farms area along Highway 45 in Noxubee County.

Authorities said both pilots ejected safely following the crash.

Additional details, including what led to the crash, were not immediately available.

item.title: Mississippi insurance commissioner urges residents to review hurricane, flood coverage before storm season - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
STATEWIDE — Mississippi Insurance Commissioner Mike Chaney is encouraging residents to review their insurance policies and prepare their homes ahead of hurricane season, especially after recent flooding in parts of the state.

Chaney said while there is no specific “hurricane insurance” policy, homeowners can purchase different types of coverage to protect against storm-related damage.

“Multiple peril insurance is one option that covers wind damage or hail damage caused by a hurricane or other named storms,” Chaney said. “With recent flooding in the Pine Belt and on the Gulf Coast, I hope homeowners will also take a hard look at their flood insurance needs.”

According to the Mississippi Insurance Department, standard homeowners insurance policies generally cover wind and hail damage but do not cover flooding. Flood insurance must typically be purchased separately, often through the National Flood Insurance Program, and usually includes a 30-day waiting period before coverage begins.

State officials said fewer than 50,000 flood insurance policies were active in Mississippi as of December 2025.

Chaney also urged homeowners to speak with their insurance agents about changes in coverage needs and policy details. Officials recommended shopping around for coverage, increasing deductibles, bundling policies and making home improvements to help reduce insurance premiums.

The department also encouraged residents to create a home inventory using the NAIC Home Inventory App to document belongings before severe weather strikes.

Residents with insurance questions or claim issues can contact the Mississippi Insurance Department at 1-800-562-2957 or visit Mississippi Insurance Department.

item.title: Missing Jackson woman last seen after dropping off daughter, granddaughter - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – The Jackson Police Department is asking for the public’s help finding a missing woman.

Michelle Parker, 55, was reported missing May 24, according to a public notification issued by police. The notice was dated May 26.

Police said Parker was last seen Friday, May 22, when she dropped off her daughter at work and her granddaughter at school. She was supposed to attend a reporting party’s coordinated placement appointment with Mississippi Sports Medicine at 1325 E. Fortification St., but the reporting party is unsure if Parker made it to work, according to police.

Parker was last seen driving a white Chevrolet Malibu with no tag.

She is described as 5 feet, 7 inches tall and weighing about 140 pounds. She has brown hair, brown eyes and a pixie haircut. Police said she was last seen wearing a blue apron, blue jeans, a T-shirt and tennis shoes.

Parker has been entered into the National Crime Information Center as a missing person.

Anyone with information is asked to contact the Jackson Police Department at 601-960-1800 or Crime Stoppers at 601-355-TIPS (8477). In a life-threatening emergency, call 911.

item.title: MISSING IN MISSISSIPPI: Lottie "Elaine" Myers, Franklin County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
FRANKLIN COUNTY — Authorities are still searching for a Pike County woman who disappeared in Franklin County in October 2024 after leaving her home in Summit.

Lottie “Elaine” Myers, 73, was last seen around 1:47 p.m. on Monday, Oct. 28, 2024, in the 2000 block of Willis Cotton Road in Summit.

According to investigators, Myers was driving south in a silver 2015 Jeep Cherokee bearing Mississippi license plate PJ1 091. Her vehicle was later found abandoned on McCall Creek Road in Franklin County.

Authorities believe Myers was later seen walking along McCall Creek Road in an unknown direction.

The Mississippi Bureau of Investigation issued a Silver Alert for Myers on Oct. 29, 2024, noting that she suffers from Alzheimer’s disease, which impairs her judgment.

Myers is described as a white female with brown hair and brown eyes. She is approximately 5 feet 5 inches to 5 feet 6 inches tall and weighs between 150 and 170 pounds. She was last seen wearing faded knee-length blue jean shorts and a gray T-shirt.

Multiple agencies have searched the McCall Creek Road area since Myers disappeared, but she has not been found.

Anyone with information about Myers’ whereabouts is asked to contact the Pike County Sheriff’s Department at (601) 782-2323.

item.title: MEMA opens disaster service centers today for Winter Storm Fern victims - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
STATEWIDE — Mississippi Emergency Management Agency disaster service centers opened Tuesday across 13 counties for residents affected by Winter Storm Fern, giving storm victims a little over two weeks to apply for federal assistance before the June 10 deadline.

The centers, which opened today in Alcorn, Benton, Carroll, Coahoma, Lafayette, Leflore, Marshall, Montgomery, Panola, Pontotoc, Tallahatchie, Tishomingo and Yazoo counties, are staffed to help residents apply for FEMA assistance or answer questions about the process. Centers will operate Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. and Saturdays from 8 a.m. to 2 p.m., and will be closed on Sundays.

Residents do not have to visit a center in person to apply. Applications can be submitted online at DisasterAssistance.gov, by calling 1-800-621-FEMA (3362), or through the FEMA mobile app.

Federal funding is available to affected individuals across 36 Mississippi counties and the Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians under disaster declaration DR-4899. Assistance may include grants for temporary housing and home repairs, low-cost loans to cover uninsured property losses, and other recovery programs for individuals and business owners.

MEMA noted that receiving disaster assistance will not affect recipients’ Social Security, Medicare or Medicaid benefits.

The application deadline is June 10.

item.title: Juvenile charged after two struck by splat gun projectiles at Tupelo mall - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUPELO -A juvenile was arrested after two people were struck by projectiles from splat guns at The Mall at Barnes Crossing, police said.

According to the Tupelo Police Department, officers were dispatched around 3:30 p.m. Tuesday, May 26, to the mall at 1001 Mall Drive.

Police said two people sustained minor injuries after being struck by projectiles from splat guns near the food court entrance.

During the investigation, detectives identified a juvenile suspect connected to the incident.

The juvenile was taken into custody and charged with two counts of simple assault and disturbance of a business.

Police said no identifying information about the suspect will be released because of the age of those involved.

The case will be handled through Lee County Youth Court.

item.title: George County man charged with sexual battery involving child - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
LUCEDALE – A George County man has been arrested and charged with sexual battery involving a child.

According to the George County Sheriff’s Office, deputies responded May 11 to a report from concerned parents after their child disclosed possible sexual abuse.

Criminal investigators opened an investigation and determined the child had been in contact with the alleged perpetrator, identified as Dustin M. Merrill.

Investigators brought Merrill in for questioning, and he was arrested May 22.

Merrill was charged with two counts of sexual battery involving a child and booked into the George County Regional Correctional Facility.

After an initial appearance before a George County Justice Court judge, Merrill was issued a $150,000 commercial bond on each charge.

“Cases involving crimes against children are among the most serious we handle,” Sheriff Mitchell Mixon said. “We will continue to pursue these investigations aggressively and work to ensure victims receive justice while keeping our community safe.”

The investigation remains ongoing. All persons are presumed innocent until proven guilty.

item.title: Free summer meals available for children in Tunica County through July - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
TUNICA COUNTY — Families in Tunica County can receive free breakfast and lunch meals for children every Tuesday through July as part of the Summer Food Service Program.

The YMCA of Memphis & the Mid-South is partnering with local organizations to provide free meals to children during the summer months while school is out. The program is funded through the State of Tennessee.

Meals will be distributed Tuesdays at two Tunica County locations:

Organizers said children will receive healthy snacks and shelf-stable milk in addition to breakfast and lunch items.

According to program information, the Summer Food Service Program runs from May 22 through Aug. 1. Meal services will not be offered on Memorial Day or July 4 observances.

Additional Mississippi meal distribution sites and information about the program are available through the state’s Summer Food Service Program resources.

item.title: Canton repeat drug offender sentenced to 64 years on cocaine, firearm charges - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
CANTON — A Canton man with two prior cocaine convictions has been sentenced to 64 years in prison after investigators said he continued selling crack cocaine from his home while armed with a handgun.

Authorities said narcotics investigators with the Madison County Sheriff’s Department conducted several controlled drug purchases from Khadafy Manning at his residence in Canton during May 2025.

Investigators used a confidential informant equipped with a covert camera during the purchases, according to prosecutors. After expanding the investigation into Manning’s alleged drug distribution operation, deputies executed a search warrant at the home and reportedly discovered crack cocaine, marijuana, alprazolam and a handgun.

Manning was charged with three counts of sale of cocaine, one count of possession of cocaine with intent to sell while in possession of a firearm, and one count of possession of a firearm by a convicted felon as a subsequent drug offender and nonviolent habitual offender.

Court records show Manning pleaded guilty May 19, 2026.

Madison and Rankin Counties District Attorney John K. Bramlett announced the sentence Tuesday, saying Manning will serve 64 years in the custody of the Mississippi Department of Corrections.

Prosecutors noted Manning had previously been convicted in Madison County for sale of cocaine in both 2003 and 2007.

Bramlett praised investigators for their work and said authorities remain committed to targeting repeat drug offenders operating in local communities.

item.title: Body found after SUV swept into floodwaters near Petal Walmart - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
PETAL – A body was recovered Monday afternoon after an SUV became submerged in floodwaters near the Walmart in Petal, according to WTVA.

The incident happened near the store at 36 Byrd Blvd. just after 3:30 p.m.

According to reports from the scene, a white SUV was swept away by a strong current. Witnesses attempted to help a woman get out of the vehicle, but the SUV flipped upside down before she could escape.

Emergency crews responded to the scene. The SUV and the body were later found on the other side of a culvert, and a dive team recovered the body.

The National Weather Service issued a flash flood emergency shortly before 4 p.m. for Petal and parts of Forrest County. The warning was in effect until 10 p.m.

Residents in the area were urged to seek higher ground immediately as flash flooding affected low-water crossings, small creeks and streams, urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

The incident remains under investigation.

item.title: 36 cats, 2 senior dogs rescued from Corinth home after woman’s death - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
CORINTH – The Corinth-Alcorn Animal Shelter is asking for donations after helping remove dozens of animals from a home following the death of a local woman.

According to the shelter, staff worked with the city of Corinth over the past two weeks to assist with the situation. A total of 36 cats and kittens and two senior dogs were removed from inside and outside the home.

Shelter officials said the home was in severe condition, and staff had to wear proper protective equipment to safely enter and care for the animals.

Many of the cats and kittens are suffering from upper respiratory infections, flea infestations and other medical concerns that require immediate treatment and ongoing care, the shelter said.

Among the animals is a mother cat caring for five nursing kittens that are about a week old. The shelter said it is hoping to find a foster home that can give the family a quiet, safe place to recover and grow.

The shelter is asking for donations of canned cat and kitten food, clumpable cat litter, Kitten Chow, cat crates and carriers, and monetary donations to help cover veterinary care and supplies.

“This has been a massive undertaking for our small shelter, but we are committed to getting every one of these animals healthy, loved, and eventually ready for adoption,” the shelter said.

Donations by check may be mailed to Corinth-Alcorn Animal Shelter, 2407 Norman Road, Corinth, MS 38834. Donations may also be made through PayPal at [email protected] or Venmo at Corinth Alcorn Animal Shelter.

item.title: Naked man dies after strange situation during flooding in Biloxi - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
BILOXI — A man died early Sunday morning after a violent encounter at a home in the Woolmarket area of Biloxi during severe flooding conditions, according to police.

Authorities said that around 8 p.m. Saturday, May 23, Biloxi Police Department dispatchers received a 911 call from the 11000 block of Woolmarket Lake Road. The caller reported that they were away from home but had seen a naked white male emerge from the Biloxi River on their Ring doorbell camera, walk up the stairs of the residence, and enter the porch area.

Dispatchers also reportedly received multiple calls from the surrounding area about a naked man.

Police said the homeowner contacted a next-door neighbor and asked them to check on the property. The neighbor approached the home and spoke with the man on the porch, asking whether he needed help.

According to investigators, the man suddenly charged the neighbor and struck him. The neighbor then fired multiple shots, hitting the man, but police said the man continued attacking him. During the struggle, the man reportedly disarmed the neighbor and then walked away from the residence and back into the floodwaters.

item.title: JPS Class of 2026 earns more than $65 million in scholarship offers - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The Jackson Public Schools Class of 2026 earned more than $65 million in scholarship offers as the district prepares to celebrate graduation ceremonies this week.

According to JPS, the district’s 1,392 graduating seniors received a combined $65,404,367 in scholarship offers from colleges and universities across the country. Jim Hill High School led the district with more than $33.5 million in scholarship offers, followed by Murrah High School with $13.5 million.

District leaders recognized top-performing students during the annual Salute to Scholars program held May 18. The event honored the valedictorians and salutatorians from each of the district’s six high schools, along with other high-achieving students.

Additional honorees included the top 10 scholars from each graduating class, 20 new inductees into the ACT 30+ Club, four Mississippi Economic Council STAR Scholars, and 11 students who earned the Seal of Biliteracy. Seven seniors also received a combined $25,000 through the Leland Speed Scholarship program.

JPS commencement ceremonies will take place May 26 and 27 at the Mississippi Coliseum.

Graduation schedule:

Tuesday, May 26

Wednesday, May 27

Officials said the coliseum’s clear bag policy will be enforced and all guests will pass through metal detectors before entry.

Ceremonies will also be livestreamed on JPS TV’s YouTube channel for those unable to attend in person.

item.title: Booneville man sentenced in child exploitation case - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
OXFORD — A Booneville man was sentenced to four years in federal prison after investigators found thousands of files containing child sexual abuse material, according to federal authorities.

Joshua Honeycutt, 42, was sentenced May 21 by U.S. District Judge Michael Mills to 48 months in prison, followed by 10 years of supervised release. He will also be required to register as a sex offender and pay $107,000 in restitution to victims.

According to court documents, Honeycutt possessed more than 4,000 videos and 17,000 images depicting children under 12 engaged in sexually explicit conduct. Authorities said many of the victims shown were between 5 and 10 years old.

The case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Mississippi Attorney General’s Office, and the Prentiss County Sheriff’s Department.

U.S. Attorney Scott Leary said the sentence removes a dangerous offender from the public and emphasized the importance of restitution for victims. FBI Jackson Special Agent in Charge Robert Eikhoff said the agency remains committed to combating child exploitation and protecting children from abuse.

Attorney General Lynn Fitch called child sexual abuse “a horrific crime” that causes lasting trauma for victims, especially when images or videos continue to circulate.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Parker S. King prosecuted the case as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative aimed at combating online child exploitation.

item.title: Two Louisville men sentenced in federal drug trafficking case - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
ABERDEEN — Two Louisville men have been sentenced in federal court after pleading guilty to drug trafficking charges involving methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl and heroin, according to federal officials.

Aaron Hughes, 33, was sentenced March 24 to 108 months in federal prison followed by three years of supervised release. Hughes also was convicted on a firearms charge.

Warren Goss, 58, was sentenced May 12 to 70 months in federal prison followed by three years of supervised release.

Both men previously pleaded guilty to possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl, despropionyl fentanyl and heroin. Senior U.S. District Judge Sharion Aycock handed down the sentences.

Federal officials said the convictions stemmed from a Homeland Security Task Force operation involving the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Homeland Security Investigations and the Louisville Police Department.

U.S. Attorney Scott Leary said authorities have “zero tolerance” for fentanyl, methamphetamine, cocaine, heroin and illegal firearms.

FBI Special Agent in Charge Robert Eikhoff said the sentences should serve as a warning to others involved in violent crime and drug trafficking.

The case was prosecuted as part of the Homeland Security Task Force initiative, a multiagency effort targeting criminal organizations and drug trafficking operations.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Sam Stringfellow and Julie Addison prosecuted the case.

item.title: Tupelo police warn about realistic-looking toy guns - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUPELO – The Tupelo Police Department is warning parents and guardians after receiving complaints about toy guns being used in neighborhoods.

Police said the complaints involve “Orby guns,” gel blasters, splatter guns and similar toy guns.

According to the department, many of the toys can look realistic and may be mistaken for real firearms, especially from a distance or at night.

Police are asking parents and guardians to talk with children about using the toys responsibly and not pointing or shooting them at strangers, passing vehicles, homes or anyone who may not know they are toys.

The department said situations involving realistic-looking guns can quickly create dangerous misunderstandings for residents and responding law enforcement officers.

Police said they appreciate the public’s help in keeping these situations from escalating into something more serious.

item.title: Tupelo man charged after fraudulent check reports at two banks - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUPELO – A Tupelo man was arrested after police said he was connected to fraudulent check reports at two BNA Bank locations.

According to the Tupelo Police Department, officers responded May 19 to BNA Bank at 2919 Tom Watson Drive after employees reported that a suspect had cashed a check that was later determined to be fraudulent.

A short time later, officers responded to another BNA Bank at 3041 McCullough Blvd. after employees reported that a suspect had attempted to cash a fraudulent check and left the scene.

Police said employees were able to provide a description of the suspect, which matched the description from the earlier report.

Later that day, patrol officers found a person matching the suspect’s description. The person was arrested on unrelated misdemeanor charges.

After further investigation, 44-year-old Samuel T. Dickson, of Tupelo, was charged May 21 with two counts of false pretense.

Tupelo Municipal Court Judge Weir ordered Dickson held on a $10,000 bond.

The charges will be presented to the Lee County grand jury.

item.title: Rankin County K-9 medically retired after collapsing during search for escaped juvenile - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
RANKIN COUNTY — A Rankin County Sheriff’s Office K-9 deputy has been medically retired after collapsing during a search Thursday afternoon for an escaped juvenile offender in Pelahatchie.

According to the Rankin County Sheriff’s Office, Deputy Ronnie Decell and his K-9 partner, Fox, responded May 21 to assist in locating a juvenile who had escaped from the Rankin County Juvenile Detention Center.

Officials said Deputy Decell deployed Fox to track the suspect, but about 100 yards into the search, the dog suddenly collapsed.

Deputy Decell carried Fox back to his patrol vehicle and rushed him to the after-hours emergency veterinary clinic URGIVET in Madison for treatment.

Veterinarians later determined Fox was suffering from an undiagnosed tumor that ruptured during the track, causing severe internal bleeding near his heart, according to the sheriff’s office.

Fox remains under treatment and observation for what officials described as a life-threatening condition. Because of the diagnosis, the sheriff’s office said Fox will be medically retired from service.

Fox, a 10-year-old Belgian Malinois, is trained and certified in narcotics detection, tracking and handler protection. The sheriff’s office said he has served Rankin County throughout his career alongside Deputy Decell.

Sheriff Bryan Bailey asked the community to keep Deputy Decell, his family and Fox in their thoughts and prayers.

item.title: Leake County deputies seize meth, firearms during drug bust - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
LEAKE COUNTY – A large amount of drugs and several firearms were seized during a drug bust in Leake County, according to the Leake County Sheriff’s Office.

Sheriff Randy W. Atkinson said deputies and investigators seized 395 grams of methamphetamine, 54 grams of spice, 10 grams of marijuana and five firearms from a home off Pearl Hill Road.

According to the sheriff’s office, the methamphetamine seized was 58 grams shy of a pound and had an estimated street value of $5,000.

One person was taken into custody during the operation. The sheriff’s office did not immediately release the person’s name or charges.

No injuries were reported during the arrest, and officials said public safety remained the top priority throughout the operation.

The sheriff’s office is encouraging anyone with information about drug activity to contact deputies.

item.title: Choctaw tribal community ponds restocked for Memorial Day weekend - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
CHOCTAW – Tribal community ponds have been restocked with catfish just in time for Memorial Day weekend, the Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians announced.

The restocking was announced by Tribal Chief Cyrus Ben and includes ponds in several tribal communities.

The stocked ponds include Pearl River Community Pond, Town Center Pond in Pearl River, the pond in front of Lake Pushmataha in Pearl River, Fani Lakna Pond in Tucker, Tucker Community Pond and Bogue Chitto Community Pond in Neshoba County.

Other stocked locations include Conehatta Community Pond in Newton County; Standing Pine Community Pond, Standing Pine School Pond and Attala Pond in Leake County; and Crystal Ridge Pond in Winston County.

Community members are invited to bring family and friends out for fishing, fellowship and outdoor fun during the holiday weekend.

Officials are reminding anglers to practice a courtesy limit of five catfish per person and to be mindful of others.

item.title: 14-year-old captured after climbing fence during recreation at juvenile detention center - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
RANKIN COUNTY – A 14-year-old juvenile detainee was captured Thursday night after escaping from the Rankin County Juvenile Detention Center and later leading deputies on a pursuit in a stolen vehicle.

According to the Rankin County Sheriff’s Office, officers at the detention center reported around 3 p.m. May 21 that a juvenile detainee had escaped from the facility in Pelahatchie after climbing a security fence and running away.

Sheriff Bryan Bailey said detainees were participating in mandatory outdoor recreation, with several playing basketball, when the basketball rolled near the perimeter fence. The juvenile ran toward the ball and began climbing the 16-foot security fence.

A detention officer responded and grabbed the juvenile while he was on the fence, attempting to pull him back down. The sheriff’s office said the juvenile broke free, climbed over the fence and ran into a wooded area.

Deputies and assisting law enforcement agencies responded and established a perimeter. Rankin County Sheriff’s Office K-9 units, Flowood Police Department K-9 units, Mississippi Highway Patrol K-9 units and the sheriff’s office drone team assisted in the search.

Authorities said an extensive ground and aerial search continued through the afternoon and evening, and checkpoints were set up in the surrounding area.

Around 11 p.m., a Banks Street resident called 911 and reported that the escapee was at her home attempting to steal her husband’s white Chevrolet 2500 pickup truck. The caller said the juvenile left the residence traveling west on Highway 80 toward Brandon.

Deputies soon located the stolen vehicle and attempted a traffic stop, but the juvenile refused to stop, leading deputies on a pursuit that lasted about 20 minutes and traveled along several county roads.

Deputies attempted to direct the pursuit toward Brandon, where Brandon police had deployed stop sticks. The juvenile eventually turned onto Mount Ridge Road, a dead-end road, where deputies were able to box in the vehicle.

Authorities said the juvenile then attempted to escape through a cutover area but became stuck. Deputies reached the vehicle and took him into custody before he could run away again.

Pafford Ambulance Service responded and transported the juvenile to a local hospital for treatment of injuries sustained during the escape. After treatment, he was returned to the custody of the Rankin County Juvenile Detention Center.

The sheriff’s office said the stolen vehicle sustained heavy damage. The owner operates a small landscaping business and relies on the truck for work.

The juvenile was originally being held at the detention center on charges of auto theft and auto burglary. He is scheduled to appear before Youth Court Judge Josh McCrory.

The Rankin County Juvenile Detention Center opened in 2011, and officials said this was the first escape in the facility’s history. Bailey and McCrory are reevaluating outdoor recreation security procedures and plan to implement additional measures while staying in compliance with state and federal guidelines for juvenile detention facilities.

Bailey thanked deputies, dispatchers, detention officers and assisting agencies, including the Mississippi Highway Patrol, Pelahatchie Police Department, Flowood Police Department, Brandon Police Department, Madison Police Department and Scott County Sheriff’s Department.

“We hope the quick recapture of this escapee provides peace of mind to our citizens,” Bailey said.
